events.name: AI Builders Week 4: RAG, Vector Search & Context Memory
events.description:
Your model only knows what you give it. This session is about giving it the right things: chunking documents so they stay meaningful, generating embeddings, and running vector search that actually grounds your answers in real sources. Then context memory: what to keep, what to summarize, and what to throw away so your agent stays sharp over long conversations without blowing up your token bill.
You'll leave with a working local RAG pipeline you can plug into your fellowship project.
Some coding experience needed. This is about applied engineering, not starting from scratch.
Part of the AI Architect Fellowship, a free program from 3percentclub for underrepresented builders in NYC.
Joining virtually? Live stream: https://us06web.zoom.us/s/84280401788
Applying to the fellowship gets you:
Access to our Google Classroom for labs and coursework
Mentorship from working AI practitioners
Resume workshops
Our Discord community
A shot at the October hackathon and Demo Night
Sign up: https://forms.fillout.com/t/p52mmdNs8jus

events.name: AI Builders Week 5: Privacy & Security Controls
events.description:
What happens to the data an agent sends, stores, and returns? We’ll look at Zero Data Retention, endpoint controls, self-hosting options, and how to handle personal information in a system people may rely on.
You’ll examine the privacy and security choices for your own project as cross-track pods form with Citizens.
Some coding experience needed. This is about applied engineering, not starting from scratch.
Part of the AI Architect Fellowship, a free program from 3percentclub for underrepresented builders in NYC.
6:00–8:00 PM · Location TBA
Joining virtually? Zoom: https://us06web.zoom.us/s/84280401788

events.description:
Join us in New York on November 13th for the NYC Physical AI, ML, and Computer Vision Meetup, co-presented by Nebius and Voxel51.
The evening features lightning talks from local speakers working across AI, machine learning, and computer vision, followed by networking, food, and drinks.
Talks will include:
Closing the human to robot gap for dexterous hands — Irmak Guzey at New York University
Building Real-World Computer Vision Systems with Voxel51 — Dan Gural at Voxel51
Location: Fractal, 111 Conselyea St, Fl 2, Brooklyn, NY 11211 (Williamsburg - 3 min from the Lorimer St L/Metropolitan Ave G stop).
